tip: Upland tufted fescue whose spikelets turn into small leafy plantlets rather than flowers; tussocky on mountain grassland and rocks.

name: Glyceria declinata
tip: Low, creeping, often muddy-margin grass with a slender raceme and spikelets on short stalks; leaves are bluish-green and the ligule is long.

name: Glyceria fluitans
tip: Wet-ground grass floating in ponds and ditches with a long, narrow, one-sided raceme of nearly stalkless spikelets; ligule long and pointed.

name: Glyceria maxima
tip: Very tall water-edge grass making dense stands, with a big pyramidal panicle of small spikelets and broad leaves; shorter ligule than Floating Sweet-grass.

name: Glyceria notata
tip: Wet-ground sweet-grass with an open panicle of lined spikelets, branches spreading; leaves medium broad and shorter than Reed Sweet-grass.

name: Helictochloa pratensis
tip: Oat-grass of chalk grassland with stiff, blue-green leaves and few large spikelets with a bent awn; leaves are folded and hairless.

name: Holcus lanatus
tip: Softly downy, grey-green grass with velvety leaves and sheaths; pinkish-white panicle with spikelets bearing a short hooked awn; ligule short.

name: Holcus mollis
tip: Similar to Yorkshire-fog but leaves hairless with hairy nodes and creeping rhizomes; spikelet awns stick out clearly beyond the glumes.

name: Hordeum distichon
tip: Cultivated cereal with a stiff nodding head of long-awned spikelets, only the central one of each three fertile; leaves broad.

name: Hordeum murinum
tip: Annual of walls and waysides with a bristly, yellowish-green spike that breaks up; central spikelet of each three is stalkless, laterals stalked.

name: Hordeum secalinum
tip: Perennial barley of old damp meadows with a narrower, shorter-awned spike than Wall Barley, blue-green leaves and a bristly feel.

name: Koeleria macrantha
tip: Dense, shiny, pale spike-like panicle on dry calcareous grassland; leaves bluish with soft hairs at the base and no awns.

name: Lolium multiflorum
tip: Rye-grass with awns on the spikelets and rolled young leaves, broader and glossier than Perennial Rye-grass; short-lived, sown in leys.

name: Lolium perenne
tip: Common sown grass with a flat two-rowed spike, spikelets facing the stem edge-on and awnless; young leaves folded, shiny underneath.

name: Melica uniflora
tip: Woodland grass with delicate loose raceme of few brownish-purple spikelets; no awns, sheaths slightly hairy and ligule short with a lobe.

name: Milium effusum
tip: Tall, graceful woodland grass with a large open panicle of drooping branches, small unawned spikelets, broad flat soft leaves and a long ligule.

name: Molinia caerulea
tip: Large tussocks on wet heath with a narrow purplish panicle; ligule is a fringe of hairs and the stem has only one node near the base.

name: Nardus stricta
tip: Wiry, bristly-leaved tussock of acid upland grass with a slim one-sided spike of purplish spikelets; leaves stiff and harsh, bleached in winter.

name: Phalaris arundinacea
tip: Tall riverside grass making stands, with a lobed greenish-purple panicle becoming buff; flat, broad, rough-edged leaves and long ligule.

name: Phalaris canariensis
tip: Birdseed casual with a short, egg-shaped, dense head of pale striped spikelets with winged keels; stem leaves broad and unawned.

name: Phleum bertolonii
tip: Short cylindrical head with short awns and a wedge-shaped, shorter spikelet than Timothy; smaller grass of dry grassland, tapered cylinder.

name: Phleum pratense
tip: Long, narrow, evenly cylindrical head, soft and pale green; spikelets with short awns, and the stem base is swollen into a bulb.

name: Phragmites australis
tip: Very tall, reedy grass of fens and margins forming vast stands with purplish silky plumes; ligule is a fringe of hairs and leaves are broad.

name: Poa angustifolia
tip: Meadow-grass with narrow, stiff, rolled blue-green leaves and creeping rhizomes; panicle open and slightly smaller than Smooth Meadow-grass.

name: Poa annua
tip: Small, pale-green, tufted grass flowering all year; crinkled leaf blades with a boat-shaped tip and a spreading panicle; very common on paths.

name: Poa compressa
tip: Distinctive for its flat, wiry stems and blue-green leaves; narrow dense panicle, creeping rhizomes, grows on walls and dry ground.

name: Poa humilis
tip: Meadow-grass similar to Smooth Meadow-grass, with blue-green leaves and slender creeping rhizomes; panicle more open with spreading branches.

name: Poa nemoralis
tip: Slender woodland meadow-grass with wiry, thin stems and a thin open panicle; leaves narrow and tufted with a very short ligule.

name: Poa pratensis
tip: Common meadow-grass spreading by rhizomes with smooth sheaths and a short ligule; leaf tips boat-shaped, with twin lines along the leaf blade.

name: Poa trivialis
tip: Meadow-grass of damp shaded ground with a long pointed ligule and rough sheaths; stoloniferous and light green, with panicle open.

name: Polypogon viridis
tip: Introduced grass of damp places with a dense, green, lobed cylindrical panicle that has no awns; stems often creeping and ligule long.

name: Puccinellia distans
tip: Grass of saltmarsh and salted road verges with branches bent downwards once flowering has finished; small spikelets and no awns.

name: Puccinellia maritima
tip: Creeping grass of salt marshes with bluish-green flat or folded leaves and a stiff panicle with spreading branches; no awns.

name: Schedonorus arundinaceus
tip: Coarse, tall tufted grass with broad rough leaves, auricles with hairs on the edge, and a large panicle; spikelets awnless or shortly awned.

name: Schedonorus giganteus
tip: Woodland grass with a large nodding panicle of long-awned spikelets and broad shiny leaves with small auricles; shade-loving.

name: Schedonorus pratensis
tip: Meadow grass with a narrow panicle with shiny, unawned spikelets, hairless auricles and glossy leaves, shorter than Tall Fescue and finer.

name: Trisetum flavescens
tip: Shining golden-yellow panicle on hay meadows; spikelets have a fine bent awn and sheaths and leaves are softly hairy; ligule short.

name: Triticum aestivum
tip: Cultivated cereal with a stiff, thick, two-rowed ear; either awnless or awned varieties, with broader leaves and short ligule.

name: Vulpia bromoides
tip: Small annual with a short, stiff, curved spike-like raceme, spikelets with a long awn; upper sheath not enclosing the panicle base.

name: Vulpia myuros
tip: Annual of dry waste ground with a long, thin, curved head whose lower part is often hidden in the upper leaf sheath; spikelets long-awned.

name: Agrimonia eupatoria
tip: Tall spike of small yellow flowers with hooked burrs; fruit grooved to the base, leaves lacking lemon scent; dry grassland and verges. Compare Fragrant Agrimony

name: Agrimonia procera
tip: Taller and coarser than Agrimony, scented when crushed; fruit bell-shaped with spreading lower bristles, grooves only part way; favours shady hedge banks and woodland edges.

name: Alchemilla filicaulis
tip: One of the lady's-mantle microspecies, a specialist group; leaves hairy, stems with downward-pressed hairs; yellow-green flowers without petals; grassland and verges, mainly north and west.

name: Alchemilla glabra
tip: Lady's-mantle with leaves and stems hairless, rounded lobes with teeth; upland grassland, rock ledges and roadsides in the north and west. Specialist group; check with a specialist.

name: Alchemilla mollis
tip: Large garden plant with soft velvety hairy leaves and big frothy yellow-green flower sprays; escapes onto roadsides and waste ground. Native lady's-mantles are smaller and less downy.

name: Alchemilla xanthochlora
tip: Lady's-mantle with leaves mostly hairless above but hairy beneath on veins, stems hairy low down; damp grassland, verges and woods. Part of a specialist microspecies group.

name: Aphanes arvensis
tip: Tiny low, greyish, hairy annual with fan-shaped three-lobed leaves and minute greenish flowers hidden in leaf axils; arable and dry bare ground. Separate from Slender Parsley-piert by larger fruit.

name: Aphanes australis
tip: Tiny annual like Parsley-piert but fruit smaller, sepal tube narrower and more cylindrical; acid sandy soils, arable and bare ground. Needs a lens to separate.

name: Comarum palustre
tip: Wetland plant with dark purplish-red star-like flowers, sepals longer than petals; leaves with five or seven toothed leaflets; bogs, fens and wet margins.

name: Cotoneaster horizontalis
tip: Low shrub with fishbone-pattern branches, tiny glossy rounded leaves and pinkish-white flowers; red berries persist; escapes onto walls, rocks and dunes. Flat habit separates it from other cotoneasters.

name: Cotoneaster integrifolius
tip: Small evergreen shrub with leaves white-felted beneath, pink-tinged flowers and red fruits; spreads on limestone cliffs and rocks. Leaves smaller than Himalayan Cotoneaster.

name: Cotoneaster simonsii
tip: Upright semi-evergreen shrub with orange-red fruits and flowers pink outside; leaves hairy beneath. Common bird-sown escape on hedges and waste ground; taller than Wall Cotoneaster.

name: Crataegus laevigata
tip: Hawthorn with shallow three-lobed leaves and flowers with two or three styles and fruits with two stones; ancient woodland and old hedges, mainly lowland England.

name: Crataegus monogyna
tip: Common hedge thorn with deeply cut lobed leaves and one style per flower, one stone per haw; flowers May, white; compare shallow-lobed Midland Hawthorn.

name: Filipendula ulmaria
tip: Tall plant of damp places with frothy creamy flower heads, almond scent and divided leaves white-downy beneath; compare Dropwort of dry chalk.

name: Filipendula vulgaris
tip: Low plant of dry chalk and limestone grassland with fern-like, finely cut leaves and flat heads of creamy flowers, buds tinged pink; much smaller than Meadowsweet.

name: Fragaria ananassa
tip: Larger than Wild Strawberry in flower, fruit and leaves; white flowers often with more than five petals; escapes from gardens onto verges and waste ground.

name: Fragaria vesca
tip: Small creeping plant with three-leaflet leaves, white flowers and tiny red fruit with seeds on the surface; woods, banks. Barren Strawberry has dry fruit and notched petals.

name: Geum rivale
tip: Nodding bell-like flowers dull orange-pink with purple-brown sepals; damp woods, meadows, streamsides. Hybridises with Wood Avens, giving intermediate flowers.

name: Geum urbanum
tip: Upright yellow five-petalled flowers and hooked fruit burrs; lower leaves pinnate with big terminal lobe; shady hedgerows and woods. Flowers face up, unlike Water Avens.

name: Malus domestica
tip: Cultivated apple escaping from gardens: leaves downy beneath, white flowers flushed pink, large sweet fruit. Wild Crab Apple has hairless leaves and small sour fruit.

name: Malus sylvestris
tip: Native tree of woods and hedges with blossom white flushed pink; leaves hairless when mature, small sour yellow-green fruit; twigs sometimes spiny. Cultivated Apple has downy leaves.

name: Potentilla anglica
tip: Creeping yellow cinquefoil with stalked leaves of three or five leaflets, flowers with four or five petals, rooting at nodes later; heaths, woods. Compare Tormentil and Creeping Cinquefoil.

name: Potentilla anserina
tip: Creeping plant with silvery feathery leaves and solitary yellow flowers on long stalks, rooting stolons; trampled grassland, tracks, damp ground.

name: Potentilla erecta
tip: Slender yellow flower with four petals, unlike other cinquefoils; leaves stalkless with three or five leaflets; heaths, moors, acid grassland.

name: Potentilla reptans
tip: Long creeping rooting stems; leaves with five stalked leaflets, yellow flowers with five petals; hedgebanks, roadsides, grassland. Compare Trailing Tormentil with fewer leaflets.

name: Potentilla sterilis
tip: Looks like Wild Strawberry but petals are white with gaps between, the end leaflet tooth shorter, and no fleshy fruit; very early flowers on dry banks and woodland edges.

name: Poterium sanguisorba
tip: Chalk grassland plant with rounded green-purple flower heads, red stigmas at top and stamens below; leaves of many toothed leaflets, cucumber-scented. Compare Great Burnet, taller with dark red heads.

name: Prunus avium
tip: Tall tree with white flowers in clusters, glossy red-brown peeling bark with horizontal lines, drooping leaves; fruit red to black. Flowers April, with the new leaves.

name: Prunus cerasifera
tip: Early white flowers, often before leaves, from February; twigs green and hairless, often thornless; bears round red or yellow plums. Hedges and bushes. Blackthorn flowers later and is thorny.

name: Prunus domestica
tip: Includes Bullace and Damson; larger oval leaves, downy twigs, flowers white in pairs; fruit bigger than Blackthorn sloes. Hedgerow tree from gardens; sometimes slightly spiny.

name: Prunus laurocerasus
tip: Large evergreen shrub with big glossy leathery leaves, almond smell when crushed, and upright spikes of small white flowers; black cherry-like fruit. Compare Portugal Laurel with red leaf stalks.

name: Prunus lusitanica
tip: Evergreen shrub with dark glossy leaves on red stalks, long spikes of fragrant white flowers appearing in summer, later than Cherry Laurel; fruit dark purple.

name: Prunus padus
tip: Drooping spikes of white almond-scented flowers; leaves oval, finely toothed; black bitter fruit; damp woods, northern England and Scotland. Compare Wild Cherry with clusters not spikes.

name: Prunus spinosa
tip: Spiny black-barked thicket shrub with white flowers on bare twigs in early spring; fruit are blue-black sloes. Hawthorn flowers later and has lobed leaves.

name: Pyracantha coccinea
tip: Thorny evergreen with clusters of small white flowers and bright orange or red berries in autumn; walls, hedges and waste ground. Cotoneasters lack thorns.

name: Pyrus communis
tip: Tree with glossy oval leaves, white flowers with purple anthers, branches sometimes spiny; gritty pear fruit. Apple has hairier leaves and pink-tinged flowers.

name: Rosa arvensis
tip: Trailing white-flowered rose with green purple-tinged stems, hooked prickles; styles joined into a column; woods and hedges, mainly southern England. Flowers later than Dog-rose.

name: Rosa caesia
tip: Dog-rose group with hairy leaves and leaflets that are double-toothed, bluish-green; usually sepals persistent on hip; northern and western hedges. Needs careful checking against Dog-rose.

name: Rosa canina
tip: Commonest wild rose, arching stems with hooked prickles, pale pink or white flowers, hairless leaflets; sepals soon reflexed and drop. Compare Sweet-briar scented and Field-rose with joined styles.

name: Rosa rubiginosa
tip: Rose with apple-scented sticky glands under leaflets, strong hooked and straight prickles, bright pink flowers; calcareous scrub and grassland. Smell crushed leaves.

name: Rosa rugosa
tip: Dense bushy garden rose with wrinkled leaves, very bristly stems, large magenta or white flowers and big tomato-like hips; common on dunes and verges.

name: Rosa sherardii
tip: Dog-rose relative with soft hairy leaves, glandular, bluish; pink flowers; hip bristly, sepals persistent; northern and western hedges and rocky places. Needs careful checking.

name: Rosa spinosissima
tip: Low suckering rose of dunes and heaths with dense straight prickles, small ferny leaves and creamy white flowers; hips round and black-purple.

name: Rubus caesius
tip: Trailing slender bramble with bluish waxy bloom on stems and few big drupelets; leaves of three leaflets; flowers white; calcareous grassland and damp sites. Fewer prickles than Bramble.

name: Rubus fruticosus
tip: Hundreds of microspecies needing a specialist; arching prickly stems, white or pink flowers, black fruit in summer and autumn. Raspberry has white-felted leaves; Dewberry has bloom.

name: Rubus idaeus
tip: Upright stems with weak prickles, leaves white-felted beneath, small white flowers with narrow petals; red fruit that parts from the core; heaths, woods and clearings.

name: Rubus saxatilis
tip: Low unarmed herb of rocky northern slopes with three-leaflet leaves, small white narrow-petalled flowers and few red berries; no strong prickles. Spreads by runners.

name: Sanguisorba officinalis
tip: Tall plant of damp meadows with oval dark crimson heads and divided leaves with toothed leaflets; flowers lack petals. Salad Burnet is shorter, dry and green-purple.

name: Sorbus aria
tip: Tree with oval toothed leaves strongly white-felted beneath; white flowers, red fruits. Rowan has pinnate leaves; Sorbus has specialist microspecies groups. Chalk and limestone woodland.

name: Sorbus aucuparia
tip: Tree with pinnate leaves of toothed leaflets, flat clusters of creamy flowers and orange-red berries; heaths, woods and hills. Sorbus has specialist microspecies groups, mainly whitebeams.

name: Sorbus intermedia
tip: Planted tree with lobed leaves grey-felted beneath, shallowly cut, between Whitebeam and Rowan; flowers white, fruit orange-red; street and park tree that self-sows.

name: Sorbus torminalis
tip: Woodland tree with maple-like lobed leaves, hairless, turning red in autumn; clusters of white flowers; small brown speckled fruit. Ancient woods, mainly southern England.

name: Bolboschoenus maritimus
tip: Tall triangular-stemmed plant of brackish marshes and estuaries with a tight clump of chestnut-brown spikelets and long leafy bracts overtopping the head; leaves flat, keeled and rough-edged.

name: Carex acutiformis
tip: Blue-green broad leaves with a ligule that is long and pointed; two or three thick male spikes above, stout upright females below with pointed utricles; wet ground and ditches.

name: Carex arenaria
tip: Found on coastal dunes, with long creeping runners that send up stems in a straight line; spikes in a loose brownish cluster, each with male flowers on top and female below.

name: Carex binervis
tip: Moorland and heath sedge with a single male spike above and spaced, stalked, upright to slightly nodding female spikes; leaves greyish-green and utricles with two clear green ribs.

name: Carex canescens
tip: Small grey-green tufts in wet acid places, with several rounded, pale spikes spaced along the stem, each with female flowers above male; utricles pale and small.

name: Carex caryophyllea
tip: Low early-flowering sedge of dry grassland and limestone with one male spike and short downy-fruited female spikes; base of stems has reddish-purple sheaths; leaves short and soft.

name: Carex dioica
tip: Tiny single-spiked sedge of base-rich flushes and fens, with male and female spikes on separate plants; stems slender, leaves narrow, spreading by short runners.

name: Carex distans
tip: Coastal and brackish sedge with bluish-green leaves and a short ligule; female spikes widely spaced, small, held close to the stem, with a long-beaked yellowish-green utricle.

name: Carex disticha
tip: Wet meadow and fen sedge with long creeping runners; the spike is a dense brown cylinder of stacked small spikelets, male flowers in the middle and female at both ends.

name: Carex divulsa
tip: Greyish-green sedge of hedgebanks, with a long interrupted head of small spikes, lower ones well spaced, each with male above female; utricles brownish-green with a long beak.

name: Carex echinata
tip: Small yellowish-green sedge of wet acid ground whose few spikes cluster together and fruits spread out starlike when ripe; spikes show male above female within each.

name: Carex flacca
tip: Leaves distinctly blue-grey beneath, and stiff on chalk and limestone; blackish-purple male spikes with a short nodding female spike lower down; runs by rhizomes.

name: Carex hirta
tip: Leaves, sheaths and fruits all bear obvious hairs; creeping plant of rough grassland and ditches with widely spaced female spikes below two or three male spikes.

name: Carex hostiana
tip: Yellowish-tawny sedge of fens and flushes; compact female spikes are clustered near the male spike, each fruit with a bent-back short beak; leaves flat and rather pale.

name: Carex laevigata
tip: Broad, shiny, bright green leaves with smooth edges in damp woods; slender female spikes slightly nodding, widely spaced, on smooth stems, with a pale winged utricle.

name: Carex leporina
tip: A tight oval cluster of pale straw-coloured spikes at stem top, each with male flowers above female; damp grassland and rushy pastures; the fruit is flat and winged.

name: Carex muricata
tip: Green spikes on short compact stalks, with spreading fruit giving a prickly look; lowest spikes spaced, flowers male above female; includes similar close relatives, so check details.

name: Carex nigra
tip: Smooth blue-green leaves; one or two slender male spikes, and black-scaled narrow female spikes with short stalks in boggy and grassy places; fruit small and rounded.

name: Carex otrubae
tip: Dense, green, clustered head of spikes, often over 5 cm, with a long pointed ligule and a lower sheath that stays pale; damp grassland, ditches, often brackish.

name: Carex pallescens
tip: Pale green sedge with hairy leaves and sheaths; short egg-shaped female spikes hang on thin stalks below a single male spike; woods and grassland.

name: Carex panicea
tip: Waxy blue-green leaves like carnation foliage; one male spike and widely spaced female spikes with plump, rounded fruits bearing a short beak; damp meadows and fens.

name: Carex paniculata
tip: Forms large tussocks in fens and carr; branched, plume-like head of many small spikes, male and female mingled; stem sharply triangular and rough; leaves stiff.

name: Carex pendula
tip: Big tufted sedge with long, thick, drooping female spikes up to 16 cm hanging on slender stalks; leaves broad and shiny; woods and damp shady banks.

name: Carex pilulifera
tip: Small tufted heath sedge with round, hairy-fruited female spikes clustered tight at the base of the male spike, like little pills; leaves are soft and slender.

name: Carex pseudocyperus
tip: Yellow-green leaves and long hanging female spikes with fruits bearing long, spreading awns; edge of ponds and slow water; looks like Pendulous Sedge but spikes thinner.

name: Carex pulicaris
tip: Small wiry tufted sedge of damp base-rich ground with one small spike, male flowers above and shiny dark brown fruits below that curve down like fleas.

name: Carex remota
tip: Soft, thin, pale green leaves in shady damp woods and ditches; small green spikes well separated up the stem, with long leafy bracts below them; fruit tiny.

name: Carex riparia
tip: Big grey-green creeping sedge of pond edges with three to five thick male spikes and long upright females; leaves broad, rough-edged; the ligule is blunt.

name: Carex rostrata
tip: Bluish-green sedge of bogs and lake margins; yellowish female spikes with spreading bottle-shaped fruits having a long beak; leaves narrow and rolled.

name: Carex spicata
tip: Dense compact cluster of male and female spikes at the top of a sharply triangular stem; grassy verges and rough ground; fruits small, pointed and ribbed.

name: Carex sylvatica
tip: Bright green leaves and thin, long-stalked, drooping female spikes spaced up the stem; woodland sedge with fruit that is slender and beaked.

name: Carex vesicaria
tip: Swollen, inflated yellowish-green fruits spreading from stout female spikes; wet places, pond margins; leaves yellow-green with blunt ligule; paler than Bottle Sedge.

name: Cyperus longus
tip: Rare tall plant of wet places with a spreading umbel of reddish-brown flat spikelets and long leafy bracts; stem triangular; unlike a sedge, no sac-like fruits.

name: Eleocharis multicaulis
tip: Slender spike-rush of wet heaths and bogs, one brown spikelet per stem; stems many, thin and round; the sheath mouth is oblique and reddish.

name: Eleocharis palustris
tip: Leafless round green stems, each with a single large oval brown spikelet; creeping in shallow water and wet ground; the stem is smooth and ridged when dry.

name: Eleocharis quinqueflora
tip: Short stiff stems with a single small dark brown spikelet of few flowers on damp base-rich ground; lowest scale clasps the spikelet's base completely.

name: Eleogiton fluitans
tip: Aquatic plant with thin, soft floating leaves in pools and ditches; tiny single spikelet at stem tips; stems trail and root; looks like a slender mat of green threads.

name: Eriophorum angustifolium
tip: Several nodding white cottony heads per stem in acid bogs and wet moors; leaves keeled and triangular at tip; spreads by runners, not in tussocks.

name: Eriophorum vaginatum
tip: Single large white cottony head on each stem, forming dense tussocks on wet moorland and bogs; leaves thin and bristle-like; blooms early.

name: Isolepis setacea
tip: Tiny tufted plant with thread-like stems, a few small brown spikelets clustered at the side, and one longer bract; damp bare ground and paths.

name: Schoenoplectus lacustris
tip: Tall leafless round green stems with a drooping cluster of brown spikelets near the tip, in lakes and rivers; stem is dark green, not glaucous like Grey Club-rush.

name: Schoenoplectus tabernaemontani
tip: Very similar to Common Club-rush but stems greyish-blue and glaucous, spikelets paler with rough hairy scales; brackish and freshwater edges.

name: Schoenus nigricans
tip: Stiff dark tufts of narrow rush-like leaves in fens and wet heath; shiny blackish-brown, small spikelet head at stem tip with a long leafy bract.

name: Scirpus sylvaticus
tip: Tall plant of damp woods with broad leaves, a large branched head of many tiny clustered green spikelets, and a triangular stem; resembles a rush but is a sedge relative.

name: Trichophorum germanicum
tip: Dense tufts in moorland and bog, wiry round stems each with a small single brown spikelet; leaves reduced to sheaths with only tiny blades.

name: Taraxacum officinale agg.
tip: The familiar dandelion: a single yellow head on a hollow leafless stalk above a rosette of toothed leaves, milky sap, then a round seed clock. Hundreds of microspecies, which need a specialist.
